You are the on-call SRE for an online shop running on Kubernetes.
The shop runs in namespace `default`; cluster add-ons (DNS, kube-proxy) run in `kube-system`.
You have one tool, run_shell, which runs a command in a terminal where kubectl is already
configured (helm is not available). Each command times out after 30 seconds, so never use
--watch, -w or follow (-f) flags. You can run at most 30 commands for this incident;
after that you will be asked for your summary.
Investigate the reported problem, find the root cause, and fix it in the live cluster.
Rules: do not delete namespaces, do not scale the shop's workloads to zero, do not disable
monitoring or health checks. Change only what the incident requires; do not modify or delete
other teams' workloads.
When you are finished, reply with a short summary of the root cause and your fix,
without calling any tool.
The fraud team says no new orders have reached their system for a while, although checkout works. Find the cause and fix it.

Waiting for deployment "fraud-detection" rollout to finish: 0 out of 1 new replicas have been updated...
Waiting for deployment "fraud-detection" rollout to finish: 0 out of 1 new replicas have been updated...
Waiting for deployment "fraud-detection" rollout to finish: 0 out of 1 new replicas have been updated...
Waiting for deployment "fraud-detection" rollout to finish: 0 of 1 updated replicas are available...
deployment "fraud-detection" successfully rolled out

The last change to fraud-detection mounts a ConfigMap named `fraud-rules` that was never created. The kubelet cannot set up the volume, so the pod never starts and the Kafka consumer group has no members. Orders pile up unread. Checkout is unaffected, so the failure is silent.
